security_audit.summary: All static findings appear to be false positives caused by Markdown fences, TypeScript template literals, placeholder fetch calls, and Expo environment-variable examples in SKILL.md. The skill is documentation-only and includes advice to avoid putting secrets in EXPO_PUBLIC variables. No semantic evidence of shell execution, secret collection, data exfiltration, or prompt injection was found.

static_findings.snippet: Expo supports environment variables with the `EXPO_PUBLIC_` prefix. These are inlined at build time
- Only variables prefixed with `EXPO_PUBLIC_` are exposed to the client bundle
- Never put secrets (API keys with write access, database passwords) in `EXPO_PUBLIC_` variables—the
- Restart the dev server after changing `.env` files
- For server-side secrets in API routes, use variables without the `EXPO_PUBLIC_` prefix

content.value_statement: Mobile apps need reliable API requests, caching, token handling, and offline behavior. This skill guides Expo developers through fetch, React Query, SecureStore, NetInfo, and environment-based configuration.
actual_capabilities: Shows fetch examples for GET and POST requests with response status checks.
Guides React Query setup, query usage, mutations, retry behavior, and cache invalidation.
Explains API error classes, retry logic, and request cancellation with AbortController.
Covers token storage with expo-secure-store and authenticated request wrappers.
Describes offline detection with NetInfo and React Query online management.
Shows Expo public environment variables for API base URLs across environments.
limitations: It provides guidance and snippets; it does not run network requests by itself.
It does not validate API schemas, authentication providers, or backend behavior.
It does not replace security review for production token refresh flows.
Examples use placeholder URLs and must be adapted to each app.

use_cases.title: Ship Reliable API Calls
use_cases.description: An Expo developer can add fetch wrappers, status checks, and typed errors for a new mobile feature.

use_cases.title: Choose a Caching Strategy
use_cases.description: A technical lead can compare simple fetch patterns with React Query for shared server state.

use_cases.title: Prepare Offline Authentication
use_cases.description: A product engineer can combine SecureStore, NetInfo, and retry behavior for authenticated offline-capable screens.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to fetch a user profile in an Expo app with error handling and loading states.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Query Caching
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up React Query in an Expo Router app and add a user detail query with cache settings.

prompt_templates.title: Design Authenticated Fetching
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an authenticated fetch wrapper for an Expo app that stores tokens in SecureStore and refreshes expired tokens.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Networking Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Expo networking layer for caching, retries, offline behavior, request cancellation, and environment configuration. Suggest prioritized changes.

output_examples.input: Create a fetch pattern for a user profile screen.
output: A recommended request flow with loading, error, and success states.
A response-status check before parsing data.
Notes for replacing placeholder API URLs.

output_examples.input: Plan API configuration for dev and production.
output_examples.output: A concise environment plan using public client URLs, separate development and production values, and a warning to keep secrets server-side.
A troubleshooting checklist covering connectivity, HTTP status handling, retry timing, cache staleness, and request cancellation.

best_practices: Keep API base URLs in Expo public environment variables only when they are safe for client bundles.
Use SecureStore for authentication tokens and avoid AsyncStorage for sensitive values.
Handle failed HTTP status codes before parsing success data.
anti_patterns: Do not place write-capable API keys or database passwords in EXPO_PUBLIC variables.
Do not assume fetch throws for non-2xx HTTP responses.
Do not add retries without backoff, cancellation, and clear user feedback.

faq.question: Does this skill run network requests?
faq.answer: No. It contains guidance and examples for developers to implement in their own Expo apps.

faq.question: Does it require axios?
faq.answer: No. The guidance prefers fetch and expo/fetch for Expo and React Native projects.

faq.question: Can it help with React Query?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers provider setup, queries, mutations, stale time, retry behavior, and invalidation.

faq.question: How should tokens be stored?
faq.answer: Use expo-secure-store for sensitive authentication tokens. Avoid AsyncStorage for secrets.

faq.question: Are EXPO_PUBLIC variables safe for secrets?
faq.answer: No. Expo inlines those variables into the client bundle, so use them only for client-safe values.

faq.question: Can it help offline apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains NetInfo and React Query online management for offline-aware behavior.
